request.spec:
The trim rule now applies once over the whole tree: the consolidated due-total and overdue-total
leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure over all people of the tree
when three or more have one, instead of adding up each sheet's trimmed total. The consolidated
people count counts each person once across the tree: people whose names or aliases match (as names
are compared) are one person.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The trim rule now applies once over the whole tree: the consolidated due-total and overdue-total
leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure over all people of the tree
when three or more have one, instead of adding up each sheet's trimmed total. The consolidated
people count counts each person once across the tree: people whose names or aliases match (as names
are compared) are one person.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've made the change, and 3 of the 4 tests pass. The fourth ("scenario 2") fails on one plan check that has nothing to do with consolidation, and I left it alone.

**What changed**
- **Server** (`rollup/ConsolidatedService.java`): the descendants' figures now carry each person's own due-total (people showing n/a are left out), overdue-total and name keys. The due-total and overdue-total trim the single highest and lowest figure once, over every person in the tree. The people count treats people whose name or alias matches (case and surrounding spaces ignored) as one person, including through chains of matches. The "as of an earlier date" view uses the same logic and includes the sheet's own people.
- **Front end** (`people.service.ts`, `people.ts`): the consolidated figures combine the sheet's own people with those per-person lists, then trim once and count distinct people. Before, they added each sheet's already-trimmed totals and counts. The live screen still updates the sheet's own part straight away.
- In the first test, the two people named Ada count as one person (5 people), but each keeps their own due figure in the trim. That gives the expected 9.00; merging them would have given 7.00.

**Test results (`bin/e2e`)**
- Every consolidated check passes, in all four tests.
- Scenario 2 fails at `acceptance.spec.ts:1256`. Ben's plan was paused on the sheet's today (2026-04-05), and the test expects its next dates to show `2026-04-30`. The app shows nothing, because a paused plan skips every plan date from the pause onwards. The app's schema notes, server and front end all describe that rule. I didn't touch any plan code, so this was already the case before my change.
- The steps after that line never ran, so I compared the run's audit log by hand: it matches the test's expected audit lines for that sheet exactly.

**Decision for you:** the test only passes if an open pause stops skipping its dates in the next-dates list, while still blocking claim generation. That reverses the plan pause behaviour the app documents and is outside this change, so I didn't guess at it. Tell me if you want it, or if that test line is wrong.
